page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an ARM64 architecture powered by a 48-core Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is fully dedicated with one thread per physical core, meaning there is no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Additionally, the server includes 1843 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance scoring in the top 25% at 85110.68. Software compilation tasks also perform strongly, as evidenced by a Geekbench clang compilation score of 39488.0. Redis SET operations are highly efficient, reaching 61.96 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is a relative tradeoff; the Geekbench single-core score of 1121.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression of 8.9 GB/sec fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only large block speeds at 175.53 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 76.31 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture offers high resource density and power efficiency, translating to a lower cost profile per core compared to traditional x86 architectures for multi-threaded workloads. The combination of 48 dedicated physical cores, 192 GB of RAM, and 1843 GB of local storage makes this server suitable for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and software compilation pipelines. It is less suited for workloads heavily dependent on single-threaded execution speed or large-scale LLM prompt processing.
